config_lineage.rule: Every parent value is unchanged. This file only ADDS models, arms, nulls and blocks. Completed Phase 2 outputs and the earlier exploratory E1/E3 outputs are never modified.

scientific_questions.Q1: Does observation timing change detection at matched observation count? (established in Phase 2 P1; replicated here on fresh seeds and decomposed)
scientific_questions.Q2: Can preprocessing irregular observations into regular representations recover detection, and at what false-alarm cost?
scientific_questions.Q3: Does a timing-aware significance test (ou_ss) detect better than timestamp-blind tests (ar1, shuffle) under irregular sampling, at controlled false-alarm rates?

stable_slow_0.2.latent: stationary OU, theta fixed 0.2, mu 0, sigma 0.3, X(0) ~ N(0, sigma^2/(2*0.2))
stable_slow_0.2.rationale: median fitted ou_ss theta in P1 transition series is about 0.15-0.19; the timing effect acts in this slow regime, which Phase 1 calibration (theta 1.2) did not cover

stable_slow_0.05.latent: stationary OU, theta fixed 0.05 (= theta at the end of the ou_csd transition), mu 0, sigma 0.3, X(0) ~ N(0, sigma^2/(2*0.05))

fold_v2.latent: fold model as frozen, with (sigma_f, r_end) chosen from the grid below by the pre-specified pilot rule; r0 = 1, tipping rule unchanged
fold_v2.selection_rule: Pilot seeds only (base 8,000,000), 300 patients per grid point, regular_N arm only, ou_ss null, index analysis. Eligible: tipping <= 5%. Among eligible points choose the one whose regular_N variance detection is closest to 50% and inside [35%, 65%]; ties -> smaller sigma_f, then larger r_end. The informative arm is never computed in the pilot. If no point is eligible, fold_v2 is not run and the fold model is reported as uninformative.
fold_v2.sample_size: 1,400 enrolled (expected >= 1,330 non-tipped at <= 5% tipping). With discordance about 0.40 (P1), the paired 95% CI half-width is about 1.96*sqrt(0.40/1330) = 3.4 points, and power to detect an 8-point paired difference is > 0.99.

new_arm.poisson_matched: Same 8 baseline observations; then k_post = N_i - 8 observation times drawn i.i.d. Uniform[15, 100) and sorted (homogeneous Poisson times conditional on their count), stream 'pm_times'; measured with an independent error stream 'err_pm'. Exactly count-matched to regular_N and informative_reduced_N, and independent of the patient's state. Defined for every schedule including smooth.

new_nulls.ar1_rep: Timestamp-blind analyst pipeline for a representation R: z = R(t, y) (the binned / interpolated series of length L); fit AR(1) to z with the frozen ar1_params rule; generate surrogate z* of length L; compute the window statistics directly on z* (z* is not re-binned). For index this equals the frozen ar1. For fixed_time|W the representation is the raw series on its own timestamps, so ar1_rep is the frozen ar1 (surrogate in observation order assigned to the observed timestamps).
new_nulls.shuffle_rep: As ar1_rep but z* = random permutation of z.

inference.detection: Kendall tau-a > 0 and plus-one Monte Carlo p < 0.05, 200 surrogates; not evaluable (< 6 valid windows) = not detected (frozen)
inference.false_alarm: detection under a model with no transition (stable, stable_slow, level_drop_only, noise_only)
inference.calibration_test: exact binomial TOST, equivalence bounds 2.5% and 7.5%, alpha 0.05 (90% Clopper-Pearson inside the bounds) - frozen rule
inference.paired_ci: patient-level paired bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, percentile; Newcombe (1998) matched-pair score interval as cross-check (frozen)
inference.confirmatory_fwer: Bonferroni over H1 and H2: each judged on its two-sided 97.5% CI (family-wise alpha 0.05)
inference.secondary: 95% CIs, labelled unadjusted; Holm-adjusted exact McNemar p-values reported within each pre-specified family
inference.exploratory: estimates and CIs only; no claims
inference.continuous_outcome: mean Kendall tau (variance and AC) per arm and paired difference with bootstrap CI, reported for every comparison alongside detection

gate.G1: ou_ss passes TOST for variance AND AC in all three arms (regular_N, informative_reduced_N, poisson_matched) in block G1a (stable_slow_0.2, m = 2). Fail -> no Q3 claim; the H1/H2 results are reported as descriptive only.

calibration_status.definition: For each test (ou_ss, ar1, shuffle, ar1_rep, shuffle_rep, ct), arm and indicator, in each null-process block, from the 90% Clopper-Pearson interval [L, U] of the false-alarm rate: CALIBRATED if L >= 2.5% and U <= 7.5% (the frozen TOST); LOW (conservative) if U <= 7.5% and L < 2.5%; HIGH_NOT_EXCLUDED if U > 7.5% and L <= 7.5% (excess false alarms not ruled out, but not shown either: false-alarm control NOT ESTABLISHED); HIGH if L > 7.5% (false-alarm rate demonstrably above the upper bound). Assigned mechanically from the counts.
calibration_status.reference_null_blocks_for_Q3: G1a (slow regime, primary reference) and XN2 (theta = 1.2). A test is CALIBRATED for a Q3 comparison only if it is CALIBRATED in both, in the arm(s) used by the comparison, for the indicator compared.
calibration_status.reference_null_blocks_for_Q2: P5FA for ar1_rep / shuffle_rep; E3 for ou_ss representations; E2FA for ct|W30; per representation, arm and indicator.

comparative_claim_rules.Q3_superiority_at_controlled_false_alarm: Permitted only if H1 (and, for the irregularity-specific wording, H2) is supported AND ou_ss AND the comparator (ar1; shuffle separately) are both CALIBRATED in the arms used (informative_reduced_N for H1; informative_reduced_N and regular_N for H2), for variance.
comparative_claim_rules.comparator_LOW: Wording becomes: ou_ss detects more than a conservative timestamp-blind test; part of the comparator's loss reflects its below-nominal false-alarm rate. The size-adjusted analysis is reported alongside and the claim is judged on it.
comparative_claim_rules.comparator_HIGH_NOT_EXCLUDED: No superiority claim at controlled false-alarm rates; the comparator's false-alarm control is reported as not established, and the claim is judged on the size-adjusted analysis.
comparative_claim_rules.comparator_HIGH: No superiority claim from the raw comparison: the tests are of demonstrably unequal size (comparator above the upper bound); the claim is judged only on the size-adjusted analysis.
comparative_claim_rules.ou_ss_not_CALIBRATED_in_XN2_or_G1b-d: The claim is restricted to the regimes where ou_ss is CALIBRATED; stated explicitly.
comparative_claim_rules.size_adjusted_sensitivity: Pre-specified secondary analysis, run for every Q3 comparison and mandatory for interpretation whenever any compared test is not CALIBRATED: for each test and arm, find the largest p-value threshold alpha* on the Monte Carlo grid {k/201} such that the false-alarm rate in G1a (same test, arm, indicator) is <= 5%; re-classify detection in F1 as tau > 0 and p <= alpha*; recompute H1/H2 estimands and their 97.5% CIs. Repeated with XN2 as the reference (sensitivity). The bootstrap does not re-estimate alpha* (stated as a limitation).

detection_change_classification.applies_to: every Q2 recovery estimate (P5, E1/E3, E2) and every Q3 gain
detection_change_classification.IMPROVEMENT_FA_CONTROL_NOT_ESTABLISHED: CI lower bound > 0 and the method is HIGH_NOT_EXCLUDED in the matched null block, or its false-alarm result is not available -> reported as 'detection improvement with false-alarm control not established'; never called recovery
detection_change_classification.GENUINE_RECOVERY: CI lower bound > 0 AND the method is CALIBRATED (or LOW) in the matched null block for the same arm(s) and indicator -> may be called recovery; 'material' if the lower bound > +5
detection_change_classification.IMPROVEMENT_AT_FALSE_ALARM_COST: CI lower bound > 0 AND the method is HIGH (false-alarm rate demonstrably above 7.5%: 90% lower bound > 7.5%) -> reported as 'detection improvement at the cost of excess false alarms'; not recovery. This wording is used ONLY for HIGH.
detection_change_classification.NO_RECOVERY: CI includes 0 or lies below it
detection_change_classification.note: Only GENUINE_RECOVERY supports a claim that a method recovers detection. LOW (conservative) methods qualify because their false-alarm rate is below nominal; this is stated wherever it applies.

H1.estimand: det(informative_reduced_N, index, ou_ss) - det(informative_reduced_N, index, ar1)

H2.estimand: [det(inf, ou_ss) - det(inf, ar1)] - [det(regular_N, ou_ss) - det(regular_N, ar1)]

hypotheses.claim_condition: Statistical support for H1/H2 is necessary but not sufficient for a claim: the wording is governed by comparative_claim_rules (calibration of BOTH ou_ss and the comparator).

blocks.deviation: frozen E3 lists ct|W30 for 2,000 patients (about 69 million window fits). Reduced to patients 0-999; recorded as a deviation. At n = 1,000 the TOST passes for observed rates of 3.4-6.1% (probability of passing 0.94 if the true rate is 5%). n = 1,000 is the target. If the timing pilot projects more than 12 hours, a reduction to n = 500 is allowed only with recorded approval (deviations.json entry before the run). An n = 500 result is STRICTLY DESCRIPTIVE: it cannot establish CALIBRATED status, so ct|W30 cannot be classified as GENUINE_RECOVERY or support any claim of controlled false-alarm rates (TOST at n = 500 passes only for 3.8-5.4%, probability 0.62 at a true 5%).

run_order: Stage 0: code, unit tests, plumbing, identity checks, timing pilot (5 patients per block, discarded) -> projected runtime reported for approval
Stage 3: G1b-d, XN1, XN2, XS1, XR1-XR10, XS2
Stage 6: E2, E2FA (only if the timing pilot projects a feasible runtime)
